First, note that the range of $\theta =\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x$ is given by

$$
-{90}^{∘}\le \theta \le {90}^{∘}.
$$

Now, let's take a look at the unit circle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14036892/assets/d93c490adbb5cdbc0e9a09b60eea9b82ab93be8e871e334423abc17ddd62955e.png)

From the values on the unit circle, we see that

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡({330}^{∘})=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

However, ${330}^{∘}$ does not lie within the range of $\theta .$ To get an angle that's coterminal with ${330}^{∘}$ that lies within the range of $\theta ,$ we subtract ${360}^{∘}.$

$$
{330}^{∘}-{360}^{∘}=-{30}^{∘}.
$$

Hence,

$$
\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{1}{2})=-{30}^{∘}.
$$
